title: Exact Identification of Quantum Correlations in the Minimal Bell Scenario
authors: Liang-Liang Sun, Jie Wang, Sixia Yu
abstract: Bell nonlocality places the long-standing philosophical disputes over the nature of quantum theory on a mathematically rigorous, experimentally testable footing, positioning quantum mechanics between local realism and the most general no-signaling theories. Yet the precise quantum boundary has remained elusive even in the minimal Bell scenario, where the extreme points generating the set are known. Here we characterize this boundary through a computable necessary and sufficient criterion: a correlation is quantum if and only if it can be decomposed into an extreme quantum correlation and a classical correlation. The criterion follows from our proof that every Bell functional exhibiting quantum advantage admits a unique quantum maximizer. We further classify the finitely many maximal-face structures containing each nonlocal exposed point according to their local deterministic vertices. By sharply distinguishing physically realizable correlations from nonphysical ones, these results resolve a long-standing open problem and provide a new foundation for identifying the principles underlying quantum theory and determining the ultimate information-theoretic limits of quantum correlations.
summary: This work provides a definitive mathematical criterion to distinguish true quantum correlations from classical or nonphysical ones within the Bell test framework. By proving that any quantum correlation must decompose into a pure quantum component and a local component, it resolves a long-standing open problem in quantum foundations. This offers a powerful, computable tool for testing the fundamental principles underlying quantum mechanics.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously characterize the boundary separating physically realizable quantum correlations from nonphysical ones, particularly in the minimal Bell scenario.
main_result: It establishes a necessary and sufficient criterion stating that a correlation is quantum if and only if it can be decomposed into a single pure-two-qubit correlation and a classical (local) correlation.
method: The authors employ convex geometry, analyzing the normal cone and exposed faces of the quantum correlation set using linear functionals and decomposition theorems.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the (2, 2, 2) Bell scenario, involving two parties (Alice and Bob) making binary measurements on a shared bipartite quantum state.
key_observables: The correlation vector $\vec{Q} \in \mathbb{R}^8$, which captures expectation values of measurement outcomes.
important_parameters: The five angles $\vec{\theta}$ parameterizing the pure two-qubit state, and the weights $\lambda$ governing the decomposition.
main_assumptions: The analysis is confined to the minimal Bell scenario, and the core theorems rely on the geometric properties of the quantum set $Q$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the quantum boundary problem to proving the one-point-plus-local decomposition theorem, followed by detailed geometric analysis of the normal cone and the structure of maximal proper faces.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework for certifying quantum correlations provides fundamental tools applicable to understanding entanglement witnesses and resource theories in quantum information.
